newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Indonesia's Medco takes Kazakh oil company stake.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Medco takes Kazakh oil company stake.

text.p: Indonesia's Central Asia Petroleum Ltd. has bought a 60 percent stake in Kazakhstan's largest oil company Mangistaumunaigaz for $4.35 billion, a senior Kazakh minister said Monday.
Most of the remaining shares will be floated off to portfolio investors, in what the government hopes will give a decisive push to a new Kazakh stock exchange.
Kazakhstan signed the contract on Sunday with Central Asia Petroleum, a subsidiary of PT Medco Energy Corp., a government statement said.

"The gist of the contract is as follows -- the company buys a 60 percent stake and pays $4.348 billion for it, $4.1 billion of which is its investment proper and $248 million of which is a bonus to the government," Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Pavlov told a news conference.
Pavlov, who is chairman of Kazakhstan's tender committee, said the Indonesian company was chosen "because its offer was incomparably better than that of (six) other bidders."
Central Asia Petroleum must invest the $4.1 billion over 20 years, including $2 billion in the first five years, he said. It will have to pay penalties if investments fall behind schedule, he said.

Another 10 percent of Mangistaumunaigaz will be owned by employees. The government will retain a 30 percent stake, which will eventually be sold off to portfolio investors on a stock market the former Soviet republic plans to set up by the year-end, he said.
The deal gives the Indonesian company a foothold in one of the world's most energy-rich areas, although it needs billions of dollars of investment to realise its potential.
